name: Safflower (beni) lipstick

card.summary: Beni is a traditional Japanese lip colour made from safflower petals, giving lips a red that can shift to a green-gold sheen when layered.
card.note: As with any cosmetic, a patch test is commonly advised.

quick.overview:
Beni is a red pigment taken from safflower petals and used in Japan as a traditional lip colour. Safflower is one of humanity's oldest crops, and its red pigment carthamin has long been used for dyeing.

Wearers use it for a natural-looking red on the lips. Isehan Honten in Tokyo, founded in 1825, is a maker that sells beni and western-style lipsticks.
quick.how: Traditional beni is sold in small pots or dishes. Wearers pick up colour with a damp brush and apply it to the lips, and makers such as Isehan Honten sell it in Tokyo.
quick.risks: Beni is a plant-based cosmetic, and as with any cosmetic, allergic reactions are possible.

lead: Safflower (beni) lipstick is a traditional Japanese lip colour made from the red pigment in safflower petals. Safflower is one of the oldest crops, and its orange-red pigment carthamin was widely used as a textile dye until cheaper aniline dyes appeared.[1]

Beni appeals as a natural red that wearers apply sheer or build up. Isehan Honten, a Tokyo maker founded in 1825 as a family shop, launched a saffron-based branded beni lip gloss called Kiss Me in 1935 and later added western-style lipsticks, and it keeps a small museum of beni history.[2]

chain: Natural red tint on the lips
angle.text: Beni gives the lips a red tint from a plant pigment. It is part of Japanese traditional cosmetic practice.

paras: Safflower petals contain one red and two yellow dyes; the red, carthamin, was widely used as a dye until cheaper aniline dyes appeared.[1] Safflower was first cultivated in Mesopotamia around 2500 BC.[1]

Isehan began as a family shop in 1825. In 1935 it marketed a branded beni lip gloss in china pots as Kiss Me, and the Kiss Me name is still used for its range, which includes western-style lipsticks.[2]

timeline.event: Isehan Honten founded as a family shop.[2]
Isehan launches Kiss Me beni lip gloss.[2]
